findings.summary: The DROP TABLE statement for replace=True puts the table name into the SQL unquoted, so a name with a space or SQL in it breaks or rewrites the statement.
Short rows are not padded with None, so the column types and the CREATE TABLE lose columns and the INSERT does not match them.
write_sql opens (and truncates) the file before to_sql runs, so a conversion error destroys the existing file.
The table is created with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so with replace=False the script no longer fails on an existing table of the same name and silently inserts the rows into it.
